# Fuel-receipt extraction - results (generated by scripts/make_report.mjs; do not edit by hand)

Fields scored: `pump_name`, `transaction_date`, `total_amount` ONLY. Exact match uses the normalisation policy in `src/scoring.mjs`. Denominators are receipts with a label for the field (a label of null means 'the correct output is nothing').
**FALSE ACCEPT** = the record would be used with no human review while at least one field is wrong (for non-fuel controls: not held for review). **false-confident** = a wrong value on a field not flagged for review.

## 1. Corpus (what was actually measured)

| group | receipts | label provenance |
|---|---|---|
| authentic / dev | 12 | assistant-verified from the page image (NOT independently human-verified) |
| authentic / heldout | 10 | assistant-verified from the page image (NOT independently human-verified) |
| synthetic / dev | 30 | construction truth |
| synthetic / heldout | 48 | construction truth |
| generic_control / control | 24 | construction truth (non-fuel: correct outcome = hold for review) |
| synthetic / heldout2 | 48 | construction truth |
| suspected_template_generated / heldout | 1 | assistant-verified; layout resembles public generator templates, NOT counted as authentic |

**Authentic receipts cover only three brands - BPCL, HP and IndianOil. There are no authentic Nayara, Jio-bp or Shell receipts, no independent dealers with unfamiliar layouts beyond what those three include, and the 22 authentic receipts come from 7 expense reports (so they share photographers, scanners and printers).** n = 22 is far too small to estimate real-world accuracy.

### 3b. Dates: guessing vs holding

The existing parser reads a numeric date day-first without any evidence, so it can score well on receipts where day-first happens to be right, while being unable to tell a proven date from a guess. `resolvable on the receipt alone` = a careful reader can establish the date from the receipt (a component > 12, equal components, a month name, ISO). `ambiguous on the receipt alone` = day and month are both <= 12 with no proof on the receipt.

| run | receipts | date exact on RESOLVABLE receipts | ambiguous-alone receipts | ... a date was returned | ... returned AND marked usable (no review) | ... held for review | wrong date marked usable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| authentic 22: old parser + single-pass OCR (= baseline) | 22 | 13/16 | 6 | 5 | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| authentic 22: new parser + improved OCR (= final) | 22 | 14/16 | 6 | 2 | 2 | 4 | 0 |

## 5. Label-policy correction disclosed

After the first held-out look, 7 of the synthetic held-out `pump_name` 'false-confident' results turned out to be a label-design error: the jio-bp and Shell synthetic labels accepted only `<brand> <dealer>` while the authentic policy (and the brief: prefer the printed dealer name) also accepts the dealer alone. The dealer-only form was added to the labels of those two templates only; the generator, images and printed text did not change. Both scorings are shown in section 2.

## 6. Processing time and hardware

Hardware: Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-1005G1 CPU @ 1.20GHz, 4 logical cores, 8 GB RAM, win32, Node v24.21.0. CPU only; no GPU; OCR is tesseract.js (WASM); no network.

| OCR mode | images | mean OCR ms/image | median | p95 | worst | images that needed the retry | extractor ms/image |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| single | 173 | 637 | 332 | 2368 | 4554 | 0 | 1.20 |
| retry | 173 | 1819 | 504 | 6041 | 39776 | 57 | 1.13 |
